summary: Constrained speculative decoding: Core structured-output matchers inside sampled speculation
implementation_scope: Header-only C++20 adapter joining Core's request-private TokenMatcher (crit/constraints.h: finite choices, JSON objects, compiled grammars) with an isolated raw-logit LogitState into mtp-decode's ProbabilityState, plus constrained_logits and a stdlib Python host reference of the constrained law, acceptance and residual repair, (mask before temperature/top-k/top-p/min-p on mtp-decode Distributions). Matchers, masked Core sampling, the schema/regex/EBNF compiler, preparation and tokenizer byte tables are Core's structured-output service. Device masks and per-position verification masks remain engine work.

agent_guidance.use_when: A request carries a structured-output constraint and the engine decodes with mtp-decode's SampledSpeculator
agent_guidance.avoid_when: Decoding is ordinary one token at a time (use Core's Sampler with AllowedTokens directly) or output is unconstrained
provides: Sorted permitted-token masks applied before temperature/top-k/top-p/min-p with the existing token-ID tie rule
A concrete constrained ProbabilityState with private copied matcher frontiers, validated forks and complete rewind
Matcher validation before model mutation and enforced retirement after failed model appends or rewinds
Runnable ordinary/speculative example through the existing sampled controller with choice, JSON and compiled-grammar matchers
engine_supplies: Isolated LogitState forks, fully materialized prefixes, complete rewind and settled arithmetic on success or failure
Core ByteVocabulary from exact decoded pieces, the same language and token IDs for target and draft, EOS in controller stop IDs
Per-request Core matchers (fresh per request), device masks per verification position and request resource reservations
preserve: Mask before probability filters and use each model's actual constrained law for acceptance/residual correction
Matcher and model describe the same accepted prefix; discarded or failed branches never publish matcher state
EOS terminates only at a complete accepted output; absorbing terminal next laws do not authorize appending after EOS
adapt: Device-side mask generation for draft and verify positions measured against complete-round costs
Any Core TokenMatcher implementation with exact isolated forks and complete rewind

code_files.purpose: constrained_logits and the ConstrainedProbabilityState adapter over Core's TokenMatcher for SampledSpeculator
Runnable constrained sampled speculation on a synthetic logit model with choice, JSON and compiled-grammar matchers
Host reference of the constrained law, speculative acceptance and positive-residual repair under a mask

requires.hardware: C++20 standard library and Core's crit::core; optional Python 3.11+ standard library for the host reference
requires.model: Compatible decoded vocabulary pieces/EOS and a physically settled isolated raw-logit state for target and draft
requires.workload: Structured outputs under probability-correct speculative rounds

contract.input: A fresh Core TokenMatcher, an isolated LogitState positioned after the prompt, finite full logits and sampling parameters
contract.output: Full-vocabulary Distribution with zero forbidden mass, or a private constrained ProbabilityState
contract.ownership: Each state owns one model state and one matcher; forks isolate both. Core vocabularies and grammars are shared immutably. LogitState and TokenMatcher calls are serialized and settle all work before return or throw.
contract.failure: Reject malformed IDs, nonfinite logits, empty support, invalid tokens before model append, malformed forks and rewinds into the prompt. Failed model mutations poison the branch; it must be retired, not retried.
contract.core_boundary: Languages, matchers and masked sampling are Core's structured-output service (crit/constraints.h, crit_core.constraints); use next laws inside SampledSpeculator, expose only prepared output from Session.advance and coordinate model/matcher publication through successful Session.commit.

validation.host: Worked example checks the host constrained law (mask before filters, greedy ties), acceptance and in-language residual repair; Core's Python tests cover the compiler, preparation and byte tables
validation.native: C++ fixtures cover constraint-first filters, ties, private forks, partial acceptance, RNG discard, failed repair, poisoned states, malformed model and matcher forks, independent constrained ordinary/speculative answer probabilities for choice and JSON languages, and seeded compiled-grammar/choice parity; no device/model qualification
validation.performance: No model speed or quality measurement; per-position allowed sets (Core's trie walk or cache hit), matcher-history copies and dense law materialization require workload profiling
